content: 1. Administer 400 mg of moxifloxacin orally or intravenously once daily for 5 to 10 days for acute sinusitis. Fluoroquinolones should be reserved for patients without other available treatment options. 2. Administer 400 mg of moxifloxacin orally or intravenously once daily for 7 to 14 days for acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by bacterial infections. Fluoroquinolones should be reserved for patients without alternative treatment options. 3. For uncomplicated infections, administer 400 mg of moxifloxacin orally or intravenously once daily for 7 days. For complicated infections, administer the same dose for 7 to 21 days. 4. Moxifloxacin is indicated for the treatment of plague, including pneumonic and septicemic plague caused by Yersinia pestis, and for prophylaxis of plague in adults. Administer 400 mg orally or intravenously once daily for 10 to 14 days. Begin treatment as soon as possible after suspected or confirmed exposure to Yersinia pestis. Transition from intravenous to oral administration at the same dosage may be done based on the patient’s clinical status. 5. The safety and efficacy of moxifloxacin in patients under 18 years of age have not been established. 6. Moxifloxacin is contraindicated with drugs such as disopyramide, ibutilide, indapamide, pentamidine, pimozide, procainamide, quinidine, and sotalol, as they all increase the QTc interval. Co-administration may lead to serious arrhythmias, including Torsade de Pointes, and sudden death. 7. Avoid or use alternative drugs when combining moxifloxacin with adagrasib, as both prolong the QTc interval. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 8. Aluminum hydroxide decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 9. Aminolevulinic acid (oral or topical) and moxifloxacin increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Co-administration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions. 10. Amiodarone, amisulpride, amitriptyline, amoxapine, anagrelide, apomorphine, aripiprazole, arsenic trioxide, artemether, artemether/lumefantrine, asenapine, and asenapine transdermal all increase the QTc interval when combined with moxifloxacin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is necessary. 11. Moxifloxacin decreases the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 12. Buprenorphine (in various forms, including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Carbonyl iron decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Ceritinib, chlorpromazine, clarithromycin, clomipramine, clozapine, degarelix, desflurane, desipramine, and didanosine all interact with moxifloxacin by increasing the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. For didanosine, administer moxifloxacin 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine administration. 15. Dofetilide, donepezil, doxepin, dronedarone, droperidol, efavirenz, eliglustat, encorafenib, entrectinib, epinephrine, eribulin, erythromycin (in various forms), and ferric maltol all increase the QTc interval when combined with moxifloxacin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. 16. Ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, and fexinidazole decrease moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 17. Fingolimod, fluconazole, fluphenazine, formoterol, gilteritinib, glasdegib, granisetron, haloperidol, hydroxychloroquine sulfate, imipramine, and inotuzumab all increase the QTc interval when combined with moxifloxacin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor ECG and electrolytes if co-administration is unavoidable. 18. Iron dextran complex and iron sucrose decrease moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Isoflurane, ivosidenib, ketoconazole, lefamulin, levoketoconazole, lithium, lofepramine, lumefantrine, macimorelin, and maprotiline all increase the QTc interval when combined with moxifloxacin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Allow sufficient washout time for QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 20. Methyl aminolevulinate and moxifloxacin increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Moxifloxacin decreases the efficacy of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota. 22. Mirtazapine, nilotinib, nortriptyline, octreotide, olanzapine, ondansetron, oxaliplatin, panobinostat, perphenazine, pitolisant, polysaccharide iron, primaquine, prochlorperazine, promazine, promethazine, protriptyline, ribociclib, rose hips, selinexor, sertraline, and sevoflurane all increase the QTc interval when combined with moxifloxacin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable.
